question: A project manager asks Claude to map out a five-stage approval workflow with branching decision points so the team can reference it during a planning meeting. What is the best way for Claude to present this?
options: A) A JSON object listing each stage as a key-value pair, since structured data is the standard way to represent any multi-step process
B) An inline bulleted list describing each stage in one sentence, since bullet lists are always clearer than diagrams for workflow steps
C) An artifact containing a Mermaid flowchart, since diagrams are a supported artifact type well suited to visualizing branching workflows
D) A strict tool call that returns the workflow stages as validated tool parameters, since tool calls guarantee the stages are correctly ordered
correct_answers: C) An artifact containing a Mermaid flowchart, since diagrams are a supported artifact type well suited to visualizing branching workflows
explanations: Incorrect. Structured JSON is intended for programmatic data consumption, not for a human-facing reference the team will look at during a meeting.
Incorrect. A text list cannot easily convey branching decision points the way a flowchart can, so it is not the best fit here even though it could work for a simple linear list.
Correct. Diagrams and flowcharts are a supported artifact content type, and a branching workflow with decision points is naturally suited to visual representation the team can reference later.
Incorrect. Strict tool use validates parameters sent to an application tool; it is not a presentation format for sharing a workflow with a team.
